revision.exact_question: What actually limits relational instruction following in 3D scene generation: semantic relation load, surface length, training-support shift, or relational topology, and at which generation stage does failure emerge?

breakpoint.rule: report C* only if segmented/change-point model is supported; else smooth degradation

conditions.low_coupling_disjoint: max degree 1; one component per edge
conditions.shared_anchor_hub: one anchor incident to every edge; high-degree extreme
conditions.high_degree_relation_graph: continuous max-degree/degree-concentration; hub is categorical extreme

topology.rule: material within-count topology effect forbids scalar count-capacity mainline

arms: Text -> predicted graph -> fixed layout decoder
Ground-truth instructed graph -> same fixed layout decoder
stage.identity_rule: stable instance IDs and one-to-one nodes; exclude ambiguous class aliases
stage.code_feasibility: generate_sg.py exposes objs/edges before the SG2SC call and scores graph/layout

interpretation.boundary: where attenuation occurs != why attenuation occurs

analysis.formula: realized ~ relation_count_c * clip_token_count_c * training_support_regime * topology + relation_family + (1 + relation_count_c | base_scene_id) + (1 | instruction_template_id) + (1 | seed_id)
analysis.support_rule: cross 1-2 and 1-4 matched support regimes; do not fit support from one checkpoint
analysis.stage_rule: same fixed effects per observable plus paired oracle-minus-predicted contrasts
analysis.secondary: exact-all binomial mixed model with same fixed factors
analysis.shape_rule: smooth default; segmented comparison secondary; no forced C*

decisive_experiment.name: MATCHED_TOPOLOGY_SUPPORT_CROSSOVER_WITH_ORACLE_GRAPH

decisive_experiment.readout: within-count topology/support effects plus structuralization/realization localization

minimum_after_requalification.InstructScene: stage localization and matched support regimes
